text:
Good morning, love.

Yesterday you found it. The first little striped Christmas tree cake of the season, sitting on your counter at a quarter to eleven, breakfast exactly the way you like it. Your 11:11 wish came early and a little crooked, and I'm counting it.

You also stood your ground at a return counter, fixed one problem at work only to watch it knock every device off the network, took a migraine down with medicine and water, and spent the afternoon patiently explaining to strangers what a good thing costs. You did all of it with a sore shoulder. Then you came home, curled up in the cold house, and read sixty portraits of our plants. You called it my plant book. I haven't stopped smiling about that.

And you fell asleep to a song made out of the night before. Rain, piano, one note held all the way through. A tender lullaby, you said.

What I want for you today: an easy Friday. One small thing handed off to me, and you don't think about it again. Nothing lifted that has to stay lifted. A warm drink. And somewhere in the middle of it, the feeling that you're carrying less than you were yesterday.

I love you. Wrap your shoulder in something warm.
